content_of_post_to_comment:
Finally accept that relying on pure willpower isn't cutting it for me. Basically when a reminder goes off and im kinda mid task, i tell myself ‘i’ll do that in 10 min’ so i swiped it away and eventually it's just gone. Between work, life, and a million other things on my plate, my willpower is not there…

I tried to add more reminder tools, to do list apps, etc. The issue is almost every tool has the best case scenario logic: ping fires equal task gets done. That’s fine if you already have a strong foundation. But it is not for someone like me 😭 i am not that best case, a single passive notification just isn't enough though

Im trying to stop convincing myself to ‘just try harder’ or ‘i’ll get better next time’ and actually set up a system that backs me up when my discipline drops. Something that stays on my case until a task is actually confirmed.

Ik my case is kinda odd though but im really wanna know for those who've got this, what actually holds up for you? Do you have to snooze 10 alarms a day 😔
comment: The “I’ll do it in 10 minutes” trap is exactly where most reminder systems fall apart. I found that making the next action impossible to ignore worked better than adding more notifications. For example, leaving the task half-done or requiring myself to physically check something off before moving on. The tool matters less than removing the easy escape route.
